p = draw_plane(stage, where="center", x_extent=12, y_extent=1)
achilles = draw_vector(stage, p, (0, 0), color=BLUE, label="Achilles")
tortoise = draw_vector(stage, p, (10, 0), color=GREEN, label="Tortoise")
stage.caption("Achilles runs 10 m/s, Tortoise runs 1 m/s. Tortoise starts 100m ahead.")

stage.title("Breaking down the race into steps")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
step1 = draw_vector(stage, p, (10, 0), color=YELLOW, label="Step 1: 100m")
stage.pause(1)
step2 = draw_vector(stage, p, (11, 0), color=RED, label="Step 2: 10m")
stage.pause(1)
step3 = draw_vector(stage, p, (11.1, 0), color=PURPLE, label="Step 3: 1m")
stage.caption("Each step takes time, but the distances shrink.")

stage.title("Introducing the concept of limits")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
stage.equation("S = 100 + 10 + 1 + \\frac{1}{10} + \\frac{1}{100} + \\dots", where="right")
stage.caption("Total distance is the sum of an infinite series.")

stage.title("Visualizing the infinite series")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
bars = draw_bars(stage, [100, 10, 1, 0.1, 0.01], labels=["100", "10", "1", "0.1", "0.01"])
stage.caption("Each bar represents a step in the series.")

stage.title("Understanding convergence")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
stage.equation("S = 100 + 10 + 1 + \\sum_{n=3}^{\\infty} \\frac{1}{10^{n-2}}", where="right")
stage.caption("The tail of the series is bounded by a geometric series.")

stage.title("Comparing to a geometric series")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
stage.equation("S_{\\text{tail}} = \\frac{1}{100} \\cdot \\frac{1}{1 - \\frac{1}{10}} = \\frac{1}{90}", where="right")
stage.caption("The tail sums to 1/90, making the total distance finite.")

stage.title("Time taken to cover the distances")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
time_bars = draw_bars(stage, [10, 1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001], labels=["10s", "1s", "0.1s", "0.01s", "0.001s"])
stage.caption("Each step takes time, but the total time is finite.")

stage.title("Intuitive understanding of limits")
stage.clear(keep=[p, achilles, tortoise])
stage.equation("S = 100 + 10 + 1 + \\frac{1}{10} + \\frac{1}{100} + \\dots = 111.\\overline{1}", where="right")
stage.caption("The infinite sum converges to a finite value.")
intents: Breaking down the race into steps.
Time taken to cover the distances.
request: Please explain how Zeno's paradoxes are resolved by the concept of limits, showing how an infinite sum of shrinking distances can equal a finite total length. The animation should make it intuitive that accumulation doesn't require an infinite amount of time if each step gets sufficiently small fast enough. Viewers should come away understanding why convergence is about bounding the tail of a sequence rather than just adding things up forever.

prefix:

stage.caption("Start with a sphere - a few hundred points scattered evenly across it.")
p = draw_plane(stage, x_extent=4, y_extent=4)
points = [Dot(p.coords_to_point(np.cos(u)*np.sin(v), np.sin(u)*np.sin(v), np.cos(v)), color=BLUE) for u in np.linspace(0, 2*np.pi, 20) for v in np.linspace(0, np.pi, 20)]
stage.play(*[FadeIn(point) for point in points])

diagonal = Line(p.coords_to_point(-1, -1, -1), p.coords_to_point(1, 1, 1), color=RED)

cube_volume = MathTex(r"\text{Edge}^3").scale(1.5)
